$comment: The DETECTION step of the layered extraction — the fast-fail gate. It is a SEPARATE artifact from `invoice.json` because it answers a different question: not *what does this document say* but *is this document a receipt at all*. It declares FIRST of the reserved steps (`flow/artifacts.py::RESERVED_EXTRACTION_STEPS`) because it is the one step whose answer could refuse the document before the others ask about its paper. Both fields are DERIVED rather than printed (`flow/extract.py::_DERIVED_FIELDS`), so neither can earn DOCUMENT_CONTENT: a boolean has no physical anchor in the paper to be anchored to. The split exists because asking a model to read fields off a document that is not a receipt is what makes it invent them (`my_flow.md` §3, B.10's plausible-wrong-value). `comprobante_valido` is the 23-field contract's own name for this field (`legacy/prompts/11-extraction_key_value_invoice_prompt.yaml`); its `false` IS the abstention, so the enum deliberately carries no `null` escape. The partition of the contract across the five steps is verified by `test_the_extraction_steps_partition_every_field`.

comprobante_valido.description: 'true' when the text is a receipt, 'false' when it is not. A damaged or partly illegible receipt is still 'true': reading quality is the base step's question, not this one's

motivo_rechazo.description: a short phrase naming why the document was refused, only when `comprobante_valido` is 'false'; otherwise 'null'
